canonicalTextNote: voice.proposed.json is the Phase-2 PROPOSAL and the source this file was written against; the director copies it to voice.json at acceptance, and voice.json (the Phase-3 copy) is the text the voice-agent actually reads. If the two ever differ, voice.json wins and this sidecar must be re-joined against it before synthesis.

engine.name: route 2 — local VieNeu clone (~/.venvs/vieneu) with a local WAV reference
engine.note: Two kinds of control are mixed in this engine object and must not be confused. ENGINE PARAMETERS are the only two the installed clone actually exposes and they are the two that change the waveform: referenceAudio (the pinned WAV, used unmodified) and denoise (fixed false for every phrase). TOOLING PARAMETERS are applied by the local generation script around the engine and are not synthesis controls at all: seed makes a take reproducible, and silencePadding is the explicit silence inserted during phrase assembly. Anything not listed in either array (rate, pitch, volume, speed, atempo, style, directEmotion) is unavailable and is requested nowhere in this file; no per-phrase block asks the engine for an emotion. Any whole-line level difference is CLIP GAIN IN THE MIX, a timeline parameter — never an engine parameter — and no phrase block asks for one.

phraseJoinRule: " ".join(phrase.text) must equal voice.json[key] byte-for-byte (voice.json is the accepted copy of voice.proposed.json); every phrase boundary below falls on a canonical single space. Verified before generation. 33 phrases across 17 keys.

keyPlan.ownerLineFourSplit: s5a + s5b are owner line #4 split into two keys. Their join reproduces the owner's sentence order, but the break is the KEY BOUNDARY, not punctuation: a cloned voice cannot be told to pause, so 'Để khi nào rảnh.' is a separate key. The 0.20 s gap sits INSIDE s5a (pauseAfterSeconds 0.20) after 'Mỗi lần định mua đàn,'; the s5a to s5b boundary itself is 0.00 s — the two clips butt at 13.76 s. This is the single most important structural decision in the packet — the deferral must be heard as small and finished, and the silence after it is what makes it land.
keyPlan.ownerLineOneMerge: s1 merges owner lines 1 + 3 and drops the two-syllable opener 'Ngày trước,' so the hook is a two-clause sentence whose last syllable falls at 11/rate = 2.50/2.62/2.82/2.97/3.06 s at 4.4/4.2/3.9/3.7/3.6 syl/s (inside 3 s for rate >= 3.667; the 3.586 band edge = 3.07 s is stated honestly in script.md section 1.1).
keyPlan.playback: scripts/gen-voice-clone.py walks voice.proposed.json in insertion order, so keyPlan.order IS the playback order; no key is reordered.

ending.lastWordNote: s16 is two sentences with a real 0.30 s pauseAfterSeconds BETWEEN them, so its clip end — and the last word of the video — is s16Start(rate) + 9/rate + 0.30 + 11/rate. start + 20/rate is NOT the last word: it drops the intra-clip gap and would cut BGM 0.30 s before the closing sentence ends.
ending.audioTailNote: the post-word audio tail is postClipHoldSeconds + silentCardSeconds = 0.55 + 2.80 = 3.35 s; and lastWordEndsAtSeconds + postClipHoldSeconds + silentCardSeconds = 52.72 + 0.55 + 2.80 = 56.07 = benchmark.totalSecondsAt3_9
ending.silentCardElasticRangeNote: this range bounds silentCardSeconds only. The +0.40 s shrink (2.80 -> 2.40) is step 2 of the too-long elasticity set, and the +2.00 s stretch (2.80 -> 4.80) is step 1 of the too-short set. Stretching the card lengthens audioTailSeconds, so script.md section 1 must be recomputed at the measured rate.
ending.closeNeverRefilled: s16 is never re-read faster, slower, louder or with more feeling to fill a gap. If the total lands short, the fix is the tail (END card, then s16 hold, then s14 hold), in exactly that order.

pauseImplementation: explicit post-synthesis silence during phrase assembly; never inferred from punctuation or ellipsis. pauseBeforeSeconds/pauseAfterSeconds pad inside one clip; minimumPostClipHoldSeconds is a real gap between two clips in the timeline, so every measured clip duration contains speech plus its own clause pauses only. s5a/s5b exist as two keys precisely because a cloned voice cannot be told to pause; s13's beat is an intra-clip pauseAfterSeconds and NOT the owner's ellipsis.

experimentalCues.note: [cười], [thở dài], [hắng giọng] and similar non-spoken cues remain disabled unless a local benchmark proves the installed engine renders them as intended without leaking into narration or captions. limitations: REFERENCE IS PENDING. docs/giac-mo-tu-bo/voice-ref/ does not exist yet — a directory listing returns no files — so all 17 referenceSelectionStatus fields are 'pending' and no field in this packet claims the WAV exists or is verified. voice-agent cuts a 6-8 s, one-speaker, music-free, background-free WAV from vietnamese-voice-samples/previews/Thanh-Long-Nang-Cao.mp3 (which DOES exist and was recorded by Phase 0 preflight as decoding to 35.93 s) into the exact pinned path.

Reference handling: the pinned reference.source is the synthesis reference and is used UNMODIFIED — it carries no startSeconds/durationSeconds, so gen-voice-clone.py does not crop it. voice-agent must not create a second reference file under a different name: the sidecar is read-only for it, so a new filename would be invisible to the contract and the run would silently use the wrong take. If a re-cut is genuinely needed, overwrite this exact path and report it to the director.

The voice CHOICE is a Phase 0 owner authorisation (Thanh Long Nâng Cao, 2026-10-18), not an agent choice; but the reference FILE is not owner-confirmed and owner-notes.md carries no voice instruction. Nothing here is presented as an owner confirmation.

I could not run ffprobe, ls, or the pipeline audit: this runtime has no shell or process-execution tool. Therefore no duration, sample rate, channel count or codec is claimed for a file that does not exist, and no measured per-clip rate for this video is claimed anywhere in this file.

The VieNeu clone exposes exactly two engine parameters (referenceAudio, denoise); seed and silencePadding are applied by the local generation tooling, not by the engine model. rate, pitch, volume, speed, atempo and style are unavailable and are requested nowhere in this file; all pacing and intensity direction must be read by the voice-agent from phrase intent, not from the engine.

All non-spoken cues stay disabled: no [cười], no [thở dài], no [hắng giọng], and no actingCue field anywhere. s15's 'slightly amused' must be carried by timing and the mix, never by a vocal sound effect.

Silence is real: pauseBeforeSeconds/pauseAfterSeconds pad inside one clip, and minimumPostClipHoldSeconds is a gap between two clips in the timeline. No beat is created with punctuation. This is why s5a and s5b are two keys, and why s13's pivot beat is an intra-clip pauseAfterSeconds rather than the owner's ellipsis — the ellipsis stays in the TEXT and is never performed.

Phrases are joined with exactly one space (phraseJoin). An assembler joining with an empty string would merge two words and fail the CER gate. 33 phrases over 17 keys, every boundary on a canonical single space.
Naturalness, intimacy and emotional delivery are not verifiable from this file or from ASR; only the voice-agent's measured clip data and the user's optional listen can confirm them.

The 3.9 syl/s planning rate is a PLANNING figure backed by same-voice measurements, not a measurement of this video: docs/thuong-hay-so-bat-dau-lai/voice-report.md:34 reports 207 syllables over 52.6 s = 3.9 syl/s for the identical Thanh-Long clone, with per-clip values 3.58 to 4.22 (lines 17–27); docs/chung-minh-de-lam-gi/voice-report.md (same ref) shows 3.17 to 4.45. 4.1 syl/s is this repo's planning CONVENTION, not a measurement of this video, and it is therefore not the plan: the only trace of it I could find is a quotation inside docs/ban-khong-yeu-duoi-chi-da-manh-qua-lau/script-review.fidelity.md:502, which quotes a file that no longer exists in this repository — that absent file is not claimed to exist and no first-hand 4.1 measurement is claimed.

Observed floor (honest bound, not a plan): the lowest same-voice per-clip rate measured in this repo is 3.17 syl/s (docs/chung-minh-de-lam-gi). At that rate this script runs 175/3.17 = 55.21 s of speech + 11.20 s of silence = 66.41 s, and 64.56 s even with the whole 1.85 s trim set applied — outside the owner's 50-60 s window. If the measured rate lands below 3.586 syl/s the escalation is a director/owner decision: accept a video longer than 60 s, or cut an owner word. A silent cut, a sped-up take or a shortened END card beyond its declared range is never the fix.

Join obligation (timeline, not this file): the 17 minimumPostClipHoldSeconds values above (sum 5.80 s) plus the 2.80 s silent END card must be written into the video's timeline as PER-KEY holds — one real gap after each named clip — and the timeline must prove their sum is exactly 11.20 s. If timeline.ts rounds, overlaps or trims them, the identity 2.60 + 5.80 + 2.80 = 11.20 s fails and every duration figure in this packet is wrong. The voice-agent/Join step reports the measured sum, not an assumed one.

Six joins are 0.00 s, and only one of them is a KEY boundary. Five are INTRA-KEY phrase joins inside s1 ('Bạn từng nói mình sẽ học đàn.' | 'Rồi bạn đi làm.'), s2 ('Bạn đã lưu cả một danh sách' | 'những bài hát muốn chơi.'), s4 ('Sáng nào cũng quẹt thẻ,' | 'hộp thư đầy.'), s9 ('Chữ viết ngày xưa' | 'vẫn còn nguyên.') and s11 ('Người ấy đâu biết sau này' | 'mình sẽ bận đến thế.'), where both pauseAfterSeconds and pauseBeforeSeconds are 0.00 and phraseJoin is a single space. The sixth is the s5a→s5b SPLIT: s5a's 0.20 s pauseAfterSeconds sits after 'Mỗi lần định mua đàn,' INSIDE that clip (it separates s5a's two phrases), so the s5a clip end butts the s5b clip start at 0.00 s with no hold between the keys. No key boundary that carries a minimumPostClipHoldSeconds is a 0.00 s join. The voice-agent click-checks or prosody-checks each of the six on the assembled track; a click, a swallowed consonant or a broken contour is fixed by 0.05-0.10 s pauseBeforeSeconds on the second phrase INSIDE the key (or a small pad at the s5a→s5b split) — never by merging two keys and never by changing a single word of the canonical text.
